name: Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction Secondary to Mitochondrial Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction in mitochondrial disease

criteria.description: Chronic symptoms of intestinal obstruction without mechanical cause
Biochemical or genetic evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction
Imaging showing dilated bowel loops with no mechanical obstruction
Exclusion of mechanical obstruction and other secondary causes
Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities or smooth muscle degeneration

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic intestinal obstruction symptoms without mechanical cause, plus evidence of mitochondrial dysfunction and supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including gastroenterology, neurology, and genetics

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic intestinal obstruction symptoms without mechanical cause

laboratory: Elevated lactate and pyruvate levels in blood or CSF
Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activity
imaging: Abdominal X-ray or CT showing dilated bowel loops without mechanical obstruction
MRI brain may show stroke-like lesions in some cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial function
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating ragged red fibers or mitochondrial abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mechanical cause on imaging or surgery
Acute onset with clear obstructive lesion

redFlags: Rapid progression of gastrointestinal symptoms with systemic involvement
Signs of acute abdomen or perforation
references: DiMauro S, Hirano M. Mitochondrial medicine. Adv Exp Med Biol. 2017;982:1-11.
Knowles CH, De Giorgio R, Kapur RP, et al. Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction: clinical and laboratory characteristics and molecular genetics. Neurogastroenterol Motil. 2010;22(4):e1-15.
